arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Waldo argued Congress enacted an unqualified prohibition against operating new sources in violation of performance standards.
General Garre stated the expert agencies concluded mine tailings should be permitted by the Army Corps.
Mr. Olson emphasized Congress created two distinct, mutually exclusive permitting regimes for fill material and pollutants.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether mine tailings constitute fill material or pollutants. Coeur Alaska argues the Army Corps regulates this discharge. Conservation groups argue the EPA must enforce strict effluent limits.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines which federal agency regulates mine tailings discharged into wetlands. The outcome defines the scope of EPA effluent limits versus Army Corps fill material rules. It sets the standard for environmental protection of natural water bodies during mining operations.
